subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What latency threshold, restart policy, and direct-message fallback behavior should Telegram voice-message dispatch use when a source message is old by the time it reaches agent dispatch or the run aborts before a final reply?
rationale: The source-backed gap is real, but choosing a watchdog threshold, restart trigger, and user-facing fallback text is a product/reliability decision that can affect valid long-running polling and direct-message semantics.

options.title: Define a narrow watchdog and fallback
options.body: Adopt a small policy for source-date latency diagnostics/restart plus a direct voice-turn failure notice, then require focused tests and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Start with diagnostic-only proof
options.body: Add source-age logging and live repro first, then defer user-visible fallback or restart behavior until the failing boundary is confirmed.

options.title: Split remaining work across adjacent items
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86541 own sleep-gap liveness and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91652 own voice recovery delivery, leaving this issue as the broader incident until both land.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow watchdog and fallback
recommendation.body: Adopt a small policy for source-date latency diagnostics/restart plus a direct voice-turn failure notice, then require focused tests and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete appears in the feature history for Telegram polling liveness and recent reliability work, and is the best routing candidate for the policy choice among the likely owners found.
